recognize_zh: 臨床照片中左側額顳部髮際線附近（紅色箭頭）有一個數毫米大小、深色結痂的小丘疹，位於日光暴露部位；單看照片不具特異性，需配合病理與 EBER 原位雜交才能診斷 HV 樣淋巴增生性疾病（HVLPD）。
features: Clinical photograph of the left face and temple (facial features masked)
Solitary small dark crusted papule at the frontotemporal hairline (red arrow)
Lesion size a few millimeters without visible surrounding erythema or ulcer at this resolution
No facial edema or widespread vesicles visible in this view
Sun-exposed location compatible with hydroa vacciniforme-type lesions
describe_en: Clinical photograph of the left face with the eyes masked shows a small, dark, crusted papule at the frontotemporal hairline (red arrow). The surrounding skin appears unremarkable, without evident facial edema, vesicles or varioliform scarring in this view. The appearance is nonspecific on its own, but in a sun-exposed site it is compatible with a crusted papulovesicular lesion of hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder. Diagnosis requires biopsy with demonstration of an EBV-positive (EBER) T- or NK-cell infiltrate.

ddx.vs: Classic HV is a self-limited photodermatosis of childhood without systemic symptoms or persistent EBV-positive clonal infiltrate, whereas HVLPD can have systemic disease and high EBV DNA load.
Bite reactions show a wedge-shaped infiltrate with eosinophils and are EBER negative.
Herpetic lesions show multinucleated keratinocytes with viral inclusions (Tzanck/PCR positive) rather than an EBER-positive lymphoid infiltrate.
PLEVA shows interface change with parakeratosis and a CD8-predominant infiltrate that is EBER negative.
